suppress.notes:
androidx.browser:browser is the AndroidX Custom Tabs client. CVE-2008-7298 is scored against cpe:2.3:a:android:android_browser, the AOSP stock Browser application that the platform dropped in Android 5.0, and describes that app letting a Set-Cookie over plain HTTP overwrite a cookie set in an HTTPS session. This library has no cookie store and no HTTP stack; it hands a URL to whichever browser the user installed, and that browser owns the jar. The match is on the token "browser" alone.
Two report entries are the same module: the .aar and the classes.jar AGP transforms out of it. The packageUrl covers both.
Wrong if: NVD widens CVE-2008-7298's CPE set to cover androidx.browser. Any other advisory against this artifact still fails the build - this rule names one CVE, not the dependency.

androidx.exifinterface:exifinterface reads EXIF out of image files on Android. CVE-2009-1501 is a stored XSS in the Exif module for Drupal 5.x and 6.x (cpe:2.3:a:exif:exif, cpe:2.3:a:drupal:drupal) - PHP that writes EXIF tag values into a web page. No shared code, no shared vendor, and no HTML sink in this artifact. The match is on the token "exif" alone.
Wrong if: NVD widens CVE-2009-1501's CPE set to cover androidx.exifinterface.

kotlin.io.createTempFile / createTempDir used a Java API that left temporary files under the JVM-wide java.io.tmpdir readable by other local users. The advisory's own text says it was fixed in Kotlin 1.4.21; every Kotlin artifact on this classpath is well past that. The only reason it matches is NVD's CPE range, versionEndExcluding 2.1.0, which contradicts the description beside it.
The precondition is absent on Android in any case: java.io.tmpdir is the app's own cache directory inside the per-application UID sandbox, so there is no other local user to read the file.
Wrong if: NVD corrects the range - the rule then suppresses nothing and the build fails until someone deletes it - or Kotlin code from this graph starts running somewhere with a shared temp directory.

"Code execution was possible via unsafe deserialization in the build cache metadata" is Kotlin's build tooling. NVD scores it against cpe:2.3:a:jetbrains:kotlin - the whole product - so every artifact in the org.jetbrains.kotlin group below 2.4.20 inherits the 9.8, the standard library included.
Checked, not assumed: kotlin-stdlib-2.0.21.jar holds 1054 entries and every one of them is under kotlin/. The code that reads build cache metadata is in kotlin-compiler-embeddable and kotlin-build-tools-impl, which run on the build host and are not packaged into the APK.
There is also nothing to upgrade to. On 2026-08-08 the newest kotlin-stdlib on Maven Central is 2.4.20-Beta2, so the fixed release named by the advisory has not shipped to anyone.
Wrong if: the vulnerable path turns out to be reachable from the standard library itself. When Kotlin 2.4.20 ships and this project takes it, the rule stops matching and the build says so; delete it then.
Not covered here: the build host's own Kotlin toolchain, which is genuinely affected and is outside this audit's scope by ADR-0016.
